newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian government keeps strong poll lead.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian government keeps strong poll lead.

text.p: Australia's conservative government has maintained its strong opinion poll lead, despite a narrowing in the gap, a poll published on Tuesday showed.

Support for the Liberal-National government dropped one point to 49 percent from 50 percent two weeks ago, giving it a 10 point lead over the Labor opposition, which increased its support by one point to 39 percent, The Australian newspaper's Newspoll found.
The latest levels of primary support compare with the Liberal-National's primary vote of 47.3 percent in the March 2 election and Labor's 38.8 percent.
Prime Minister John Howard maintained his strong lead over opposition leader Kim Beazley as preferred prime minister, although the gap narrowed four points to 25 points.
Howard's support fell three points to 50 percent from 53 percent in the previous poll, while Beazley's increased one point to 25 percent.
But a large proportion of respondents -- 25 percent -- remained uncommitted on their choice of preferred prime minister. The telephone poll surveyed 1,158 voters around the country over the weekend.
